meta.description:
1.1. Background
This Job Safety Training Outline (JSTO) meets the requirements of DAFI 91-202 (The US Air Force Mishap Prevention Program), Chapter 14. It
covers mandatory general safety items as well as work-center-specific hazards for Civil Engineer Electrical Systems personnel. It incorporates
requirements applicable to Dover AFB, the 436th Airlift Wing, and Air Mobility Command (AMC).
1.2. Implementation
The immediate/frontline supervisor must brief this JSTO to all newly assigned military and civilian personnel prior to performing work in the shop or
field. Additional briefings are required whenever new equipment, processes, chemicals, or revised safety/fire/health directives are introduced. Work
center supervisors (NCOICs, Shop Chiefs, Foremen) will review, update, and re-certify this JSTO annually or upon any operational change.
1.3. Mandatory Items
The 10 mandatory safety items outlined in DAFI 91-202, paragraph 14.1, must be briefed and understood by all personnel prior to unsupervised
work.
1.4. Job-Specific Items
Shop-specific training modules based on the mission requirements of the Electrical Systems Shop (CEOFE) must be instructed to the application
level and fully documented prior to performing unsupervised tasks.
1.5. Methods of Documentation
Training completion is documented on the AF Form 55 (Employee Safety and Health Record) or through an approved digital equivalent (e.g., Air
Force Safety Automated System / myLearning). The form requires digital or physical signatures from both the trainee and supervisor and must be
retained in shop records.

meta.jhaNotes:
Aircraft & Flightline Environment (Airfield Electrical & Snow Removal Operations)
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 91-203; AFI 21-101, AMC Sup 1; 436 AW Airfield Driving Instruction; Latest Annual BE Industrial Hygiene
Survey.
Procedures: Strictly observe all flightline and airfield safety rules. When accessing active taxiways or runways (for runway lighting,
PAPI/VASI maintenance, airfield vaults, or snow clearance), maintain two-way radio contact with the Dover Air Traffic Control Tower and
Base Operations/Airfield Management. State exact vehicle call sign, location, and requested access route/runway.
Flightline Speed Limits:
General-purpose vehicles: 15 MPH
Special-purpose vehicles / towing: 10 MPH
Within 50 feet of aircraft: 5 MPH
Aircraft parking ramp: 15 MPH
Vehicle parking areas: 5 MPH
Snow/ice removal equipment: Safe operating speed dictated by surface conditions and visibility.
Seasonal Weather Extremes
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 91-203; 436 AW Severe Weather OIs.
Hazards & Controls: Dover AFB experiences mid-Atlantic extremes—freezing rain, heavy snow, high winds, hurricane/tropical storm force
winds, thunderstorms, lightning (Lightning within 5 nautical miles requires cessation of outside aerial/high-reach and airfield electrical
maintenance), high summer heat index, and sunburn. Dress in authorized layers, hydrate, utilize sunscreen, and seek shelter during
inclement weather advisories.
General Electrical Safety Awareness
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 91-203; AFMAN 32-1065; UFC 3-560-01 (Electrical Safety, O&M); NFPA 70E.
Controls: Recognize and respect electrical hazards including arc flash, arc blast, electrical shock, phase shorts, damaged cable insulation,
and faulty disconnects. Never work on energized circuits without an approved Energized Electrical Work Permit and proper PPE rated for the
incident energy exposure. Inspect tools, extension cords, GFCI devices, and protective equipment prior to every use.
Mechanical Safety & Shop Equipment
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 91-203.
Controls: Follow established safety protocols when operating shop drill presses, conduit benders, pipe threaders, hydraulic knockout sets,
and powered machinery. Ensure all safety guards and interlocks are in place before operation. Wear appropriate eye and hand protection.
Material Handling & Lifting Techniques
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 91-203.
Controls: Lift with the legs, keeping loads close to the body; do not twist during lifting. Utilize mechanical lifting aids (hand trucks, pallet
jacks, hoists, forklift support) for transformers, heavy conduit bundles, switchgear components, and reels of cable. Utilize team lifts for items
exceeding individual lifting limits or awkward dimensions.
Compressed Gas & High-Pressure Elements
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 91-203.
Controls: Secure all compressed gas cylinders (nitrogen, calibration gases) upright with safety chains or approved brackets. Cylinder caps
must remain installed when not connected for use. Never direct compressed gas at skin or clothing. When supporting environmental or
emergency response, review chemical flammability, toxicity, and pressure hazards.
Confined Space Awareness
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 91-203, Chapter 23; 436 AW Confined Space Program.
Shop Policy: The 436 CES Electrical Systems Shop does not operate under a Master Entry Plan (MEP) because entries into electrical
manholes, pull boxes, and vaults are non-routine.
Entry Protocol: Any entry into a permit-required confined space requires prior coordination with Bioenvironmental Engineering (BEE),
436 AW Occupational Safety (SEG), and the Dover Fire Emergency Services (FES). A current AF Form 1024 (Confined Space Entry
Permit) must be completed, signed by all three agencies, and retained on file for one year. Rescue gear (e.g., tripod/winch coordinated with
the WFSM shop) and calibrated atmospheric monitors must be on site and tested prior to breaking the plane of any manhole or vault.
Waste Disposal & Environmental Compliance
Governing Directives: DAFBI 48-101; AFI 90-821; 436 CES Environmental Management Guidelines.
Procedures: Dispose of hazardous wastes (transformer oils, dielectric fluids, degreasers, solvent-soaked rags) strictly per environmental
guidelines. The CEOFE shop maintains universal-waste collection containers for lead-acid/lithium/Ni-Cad batteries, fluorescent lamps, high
pressure sodium (HPS) and metal-halide bulbs, and empty aerosol cans. Keep all waste containers closed, labeled, and dated.
Hazardous Noise
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 48-20; 436 OMRS/Bioenvironmental Engineering Survey.
Controls: Wear approved hearing protection (pre-molded earplugs or sound-attenuating earmuffs) when operating equipment generating 85
dBA or higher (e.g., concrete saws, power tools, large generators, or when working on the flightline near operating C-5M Super Galaxy or C
17 Globemaster III aircraft). Custom or replacement hearing protection is coordinated through Public Health.
Foreign Object Damage (FOD) Prevention
Governing Directives: DAFBI 21-105; 436 AW FOD Prevention Program.
Controls: Strict tool and hardware accountability is mandatory on the flightline and airfield. Conduct 100% foreign object sweeps before
departing airfield vaults, runway/taxiway lighting fixtures, or aircraft parking ramps. Secure all wire clippings, screws, connectors, and tools in
closed tool bags.
Civil Engineer Fall Protection & Elevated Work
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 91-203, Chapter 13 & 14; 29 CFR 1910 / 1926.
Shop Application: Fall protection is mandatory when working at heights of four (4) feet or more in general industry settings or six (6) feet
or more during facility construction/maintenance, including work on utility poles, aerial bucket trucks, scissors lifts, facility roofs, high-bay
hangar light fixtures, and substations.
Controls: Inspect full-body harnesses, shock-absorbing lanyards, self-retracting lifelines (SRLs), and anchor straps prior to use. Personnel
operating bucket trucks or boom lifts must be tied off to approved anchor points 100% of the time while in the basket. Ensure an approved
rescue plan is established before any elevated operation begins.
Walking-Working Surfaces & Housekeeping
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 91-203.
Controls: Keep all aisles, electrical panel clear zones (minimum 36-inch clearance), exit doors, and shop floors free of cords, tools, scrap
metal, oil slicks, and debris. Clean up spills immediately. Report exterior ice/snow hazards around Building 615 entrances to facility
managers.
Electrically Powered Tools & Shop Equipment
Governing Directives: OSHA 29 CFR 1910; NFPA 70E; NFPA 101; DAFMAN 91-203.
Controls: Inspect all portable tools and cords before use for broken pins, frayed cords, or cracked casings. Never defeat ground pins or
daisy-chain power strips/surge protectors. Personally owned electrical tools and appliances are prohibited without supervisor authorization.
Space heaters and high-draw breakroom appliances must be plugged directly into wall outlets, never into modular furniture or extension
cords.
Hazardous Chemicals & Hazard Communication (HAZCOM)
Governing Directives: AFI 90-821; 29 CFR 1910.1200; DAFMAN 91-203.
Controls: Review Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) for all dielectric oils, cable pulling lubricants, spray solvents, insulating varnishes, and battery
acids prior to handling. Ensure secondary containers have GHS-compliant labels displaying product identifier, hazard statements, signal
words, and pictograms. Use mandatory chemical-resistant PPE (nitrile/neoprene gloves, splash goggles, aprons).
Hazardous Energy Control (Lockout / Tagout - LOTO)
Governing Directives: DAFMAN 91-203, Chapter 21; UFC 3-560-01.
Controls: Zero Energy State must be verified using the "Test-Before-Touch" principle with a calibrated, properly rated multimeter. Only
qualified Authorized Employees may perform LOTO. Use standardized locksets and AF Form 983 (Danger - Equipment Lockout Tag) or AF
Form 979 (Danger Tag). Never remove another worker's lock or tag without following the formal emergency removal procedure approved by
the Section Chief/Squadron Commander.

First Aid Station: Main hallway adjacent to Electrical Planning (Room 114) and Breakroom 111.

Emergency Eyewash & Shower: Located in the Electrical Glove Testing / Battery Room (Room 112). Inspected and flushed weekly.

Evacuation Route: Exit through nearest clear exterior door as indicated on the facility evacuation floor plan.

meta.shelterInPlace:
Shelter-In-Place (SIP) Procedures (Chemical, Biological, or Toxic Spill Incident)
Designated SIP Room: Building 615, Planning Room 114.
SIP Execution Protocol:
1. Notify all shop and office personnel to report immediately to Room 114.
2. Close and lock all exterior facility doors and windows; display exterior "Shelter-in-Place" placard.
3. Retrieve SIP Kit, portable emergency radio, first aid kit, and serviceable fire extinguisher.
4. Seal door seams, window edges, and HVAC vents using pre-cut plastic sheeting and duct tape from the SIP kit.
5. Shut down facility HVAC systems immediately (or set thermostats to off/safe setting per CE checklist).
6. Monitor the base emergency notification network / SIP radio for situation updates.
7. Check in with the 436 CES Unit Control Center (UCC) to report accountability and status. Do not break seal until the formal "All Clear"
is announced by the 436 AW Command Post.
meta.activeShooterMethods:
In the event of an active threat or workplace violence incident at Dover AFB:
AVOID (Run): Evacuate immediately if an accessible escape path is clear. Leave belongings behind. Keep hands visible with fingers spread.
Call 911 or Dover Base Defense Operations Center (BDOC) once in a safe location.
DENY (Hide): If evacuation is unsafe, seek a secure room (e.g., lockable interior office). Lock and barricade doors with heavy shop
equipment/furniture. Turn off lights, silence cell phones and radios, stay away from windows, and maintain silence.
DEFEND (Fight): As an absolute last resort when in imminent danger, commit fully to incapacitating the shooter using aggressive action,
improvised weapons (tools, fire extinguishers, heavy conduit), and team intervention.
Upon Law Enforcement Arrival: Remain calm, keep hands visible and empty at all times, avoid sudden movements or pointing, and follow
all Security Forces instructions immediately.
meta.adverseWeatherShelter:
Severe Weather / Tornado Shelter
Primary Shelter Location: Interior windowless core areas of Building 615—specifically Latrine 109, Latrine 110, and the interior Locker
Room 107. Stay clear of exterior windows and high-ceiling shop bays.

selectedModules.title: Hazardous Energy Control
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 21; 29 CFR 1910.147 - The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train authorized employees to recognize hazardous energy sources, the type and magnitude of energy present, and the methods and means for isolation and control. Train affected employees on the purpose and use of lockout/tagout procedures, and instruct all other employees on the prohibition against restarting locked or tagged equipment.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Document initial and refresher training when job assignments, machines, processes, or energy control procedures change, or when inspections show employee knowledge gaps.

selectedModules.title: Hazard Communication
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train personnel on hazardous chemicals in their work area, labeling systems, safety data sheets, and the measures they can take to protect themselves during normal operations and foreseeable emergencies.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Provide HazCom training upon initial assignment, whenever a new chemical hazard is introduced, and when new tasks expose workers to different hazardous materials. Ensure workers know how to access local SDS information and labeling guidance.

selectedModules.title: Bloodborne Pathogens
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide bloodborne pathogens training at initial assignment and at least annually thereafter, covering exposure control, modes of transmission, and protective measures.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Enroll applicable workers in the local bloodborne pathogens program and ensure exposure control plan requirements, reporting actions, and PPE procedures are covered before task performance.

selectedModules.title: Hearing Conservation
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train noise-exposed employees annually on the effects of noise, the purpose of hearing protectors, the advantages and disadvantages of various protectors, and the purpose of audiometric testing.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Ensure workers enrolled in hearing conservation understand noise hazard areas, double-hearing protection requirements, and local follow-up actions tied to occupational health evaluations.

selectedModules.title: Confined Space Program
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 23; 29 CFR 1910.146 - Permit-required confined spaces
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train entrants, attendants, supervisors, and rescue personnel so they understand their duties, hazards, signs and symptoms of exposure, communication procedures, and emergency actions before assignment.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Provide duty-specific training for permit-required confined space roles, including monitor use, atmospheric hazards, entry permits, and rescue responsibilities before personnel participate in entries.
selectedModules.notes:
IAW DAFMAN 91-203 and the CSPT lead, Ms. Bellamy, it was determined on 19 Feb 2026 that The
Electrical Systems Shop at Dover AFB no longer holds a Confined Space Program due to the lack of entries
performed yearly (less than 12). In the event of a Confined Space Entry requirement, the team will coordinate
with Bio Environmental, Fire Department and Wing Safety to establish an entry and complete Form 1024 along
with obtaining a rescue Tripod from the WFMS shop and coordinate with Shop Foreman to establish an Entry
Supervisor, Attendant and Entrant.

selectedModules.title: Manual and Powered Hoists
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 35
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide task-specific training on safe use, load limits, inspections, and operating procedures before workers use hoists in material handling operations.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use local lesson plans or manufacturer instructions to cover pre-use inspections, operator limitations, suspended-load controls, and maintenance reporting requirements.

selectedModules.title: Fall Arrest Systems
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 13; 29 CFR 1910.66 - Powered platforms for building maintenance; 29 CFR 1926.503 - Training requirements
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train employees exposed to fall hazards to recognize fall hazards and the procedures to minimize them, including use and inspection of fall arrest systems.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Cover anchorage selection, rescue planning, and equipment inspections before personnel use personal fall arrest systems in assigned tasks.
selectedModules.trainingBasis: OSHA 2254 / Walking-Working Surfaces and Fall Protection

selectedModules.title: Pole / Tower Climbing
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 30
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide climbing safety, fall protection, rescue, and equipment inspection training before employees climb poles or towers.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Ensure workers complete certification, recurring refresher training, and rescue requirements with records maintained for climbing qualification.
selectedModules.afTrainingBasis: DAFMAN 91-203 / Communication Cable, Antenna, and Communication Systems

selectedModules.title: CPR Training
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 1
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide CPR and AED training before assignment where required, and refresh qualification before expiration.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Ensure designated responders maintain current certification and understand location and use of local AED assets under the unit mishap prevention program.

selectedModules.title: Flight Line Driving
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 24
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide local flight line driving rules, markings, vehicle lighting requirements, restricted areas, and aircraft hazard awareness before granting driving privileges.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use installation or unit-approved training and certification for airfield/fight line operations, to include local speed, spotter, and no-lone-zone requirements.
selectedModules.afTrainingBasis: DAFMAN 91-203 / Aircraft Flight Line – Ground Operations and Activities

selectedModules.title: Fetal Protection Program
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide job-specific hazard awareness for reproductive health risks where occupational exposures may affect pregnant workers or fetuses.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use occupational and environmental health guidance to discuss declaration options, exposure review, and local work restriction procedures.

selectedModules.title: Ladder Safety
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 7
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train workers to inspect ladders before use, maintain three points of contact, set ladders on stable surfaces, and avoid overreaching or using damaged ladders.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Provide hands-on ladder safety training at first assignment, including local storage, damaged-tag procedures, and fall prevention expectations.

selectedModules.title: Active Shooter Response
selectedModules.reference: Installation emergency management guidance / local procedures
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Brief personnel on how to recognize an active shooter event, how to summon help, and how to apply local run-hide-fight guidance based on the facility layout.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use local emergency response procedures, shelter locations, and mass notification methods applicable to the duty location.

selectedModules.title: Government Vehicle / Utility Vehicle Use
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train vehicle operators on seat belts, speed limits, local traffic hazards, spotter use while backing, and restrictions on electronic device use while driving.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Brief operators on unit-specific government vehicle training requirements, local route restrictions, low-speed vehicle rules, and documentation of qualification.
selectedModules.trainingBasis: OSHA 2254 / Vehicle and Mobile Equipment Concepts

selectedModules.title: Risk Management Fundamentals
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train workers to identify hazards, assess risk, implement controls, supervise the task, and re-evaluate controls during and after operations.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use the DAF risk management process to discuss local hazard reporting, supervisor involvement, and integration into routine tasks.

selectedModules.title: Fire Protection and Prevention
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards; local fire prevention plan
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train personnel on fire hazards, reporting procedures, extinguisher locations, evacuation routes, pull stations, and local emergency response actions.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use the JSTO and local fire prevention plan to brief workers on work-center fire hazards, alarm reporting, extinguisher use, and evacuation accountability.

selectedModules.title: Jewelry / Loose Articles Restrictions
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train workers on removing jewelry and securing loose articles when working around machinery, electrical hazards, rotating equipment, or snag hazards.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use local work-center restrictions and equipment guidance to define prohibited items and exceptions for mission-essential tasks.

selectedModules.title: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 14; 29 CFR Part 1910 - Occupational Safety and Health Standards (General Industry Standards) Subpart I; 29 CFR 1910.132; 29 CFR 1910.133; 29 CFR 1910.135; 29 CFR 1910.136; 29 CFR 1910.138
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train each affected worker on when PPE is necessary, what PPE is necessary, how to properly don, doff, adjust, and wear PPE, the limitations of assigned PPE, and the proper care, maintenance, useful life, and disposal of PPE. Require workers to demonstrate understanding and proper use before performing work requiring PPE, and retrain when workplace conditions, job assignments, PPE types, or worker knowledge gaps make prior training obsolete.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use the work-center JHA, BE occupational health assessment, manufacturer instructions, DAFMAN 91-203 Chapter 14, and local safety office guidance to identify PPE requirements. Supervisors must ensure PPE is provided, used, cleaned, inspected, maintained in sanitary and serviceable condition, and documented in JSTO training records. Cover eye and face protection, head protection, foot protection, hand protection, protective clothing, and respiratory or hearing protection when those programs apply.
